checks.why: an edit inside a lambda in a method body is a body change of THAT METHOD, never a signature change of `Owner.<lambda>`: the lambdas of a class all carry that one name
control: an edit to the named method below the lambdas stays that method's
a lambda that is a field's initializer is part of the field: its edit is the field's initializer change
an edit inside a lambda in an expression-bodied member is that member's body: the text after `=>` is not its header
two lambdas in one method are two declarations: file:line names one of them, by its enclosing method and line
and the name printed for a lambda is a target that answers for that lambda alone
file:line on a field line is that field, not `no callable spans`
file:line on a field whose initializer is a lambda is the field, not the lambda
file:line on a class line is the class (#1426)
and path takes the class line as the class
control: file:line inside a method body is that method
